title: Newport at the Licking Mouth
summary: James Taylor Jr. settled the point where the Licking meets the Ohio in 1793, and the General Assembly chartered Newport on Taylor land in 1795.
bodyMarkdown:
Newport sits where the Licking River meets the Ohio, across from Cincinnati. The [City of Newport's history page](https://newportky.gov/268/History) credits James Taylor with founding the town in 1795. The land had been platted about twenty years earlier by his brother Hubbard Taylor, who was surveying it for their father.

## A town on Taylor land

James Taylor was a Virginia-born surveyor and landowner. The city page says that in 1793 he laid out the route for a road to Lexington, the line of today's U.S. 27. In 1795 he subdivided 150 acres of his family's holdings into town lots.

Taylor named the town for [Christopher Newport](https://grokipedia.com/page/Christopher_Newport), the English captain who commanded the ships that brought the first colonists to Jamestown in Virginia, Taylor's home state.

## County and charter

The [Grokipedia entry on Newport](https://grokipedia.com/page/Newport,_Kentucky) notes that the town followed the creation of Campbell County on December 17, 1794. The new county was formed from parts of Mason, Scott and Harrison counties. On December 14, 1795, the Kentucky General Assembly formally recognized Newport as a town. It named Taylor, Thomas Kennedy and Washington Berry as its first trustees. That same year Daniel Mayo became the first postmaster.

Grokipedia calls Newport the oldest city in Northern Kentucky. Its neighbor across the Licking, [Covington](/stories/covington-at-the-point/), grew up on the other side of the river mouth.

## Newport Barracks

The town's growth got a major boost in 1803, when the U.S. Army agreed to build a military post there. According to the city page, the army bought five acres at the mouth of the Licking River from Taylor for $1. The post became known as the Newport Barracks.

The city page and Grokipedia both say that Ulysses S. Grant and Jefferson Davis served there. The city page also notes that both Union and Confederate armies recruited at the post.

## A river town grows

By 1848, the year James Taylor died, Newport had grown to about 1,000 people. The town had a couple of churches and several factories making rope and woolen goods.

Grokipedia and Wikipedia's [article on Newport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport,_Kentucky) both trace the city's later growth through river trade and industry.

## Kentucky today

Newport is one of Northern Kentucky's main river cities, just across the Ohio from Cincinnati. Its riverfront, where Taylor's lots once met the Ohio, now holds the Newport on the Levee district and the Newport Aquarium. The site of the old Newport Barracks lies near the confluence of the Licking and Ohio rivers.
